name: crash_factors_lean_v1_1

preg_mentioned.instructions: The `narrative` states that a person involved in the crash was pregnant.

criteria.true: Pregnancy of an involved person is explicitly stated.
criteria.false: No pregnancy is stated. Children, infants, or car seats do not count.

medical_episode.instructions: The `narrative` states that a driver had a medical event such as a seizure, fainting, diabetic episode, heart attack, or stroke before the crash.

criteria.true: A driver medical event before or during the crash is described, confirmed or suspected.
criteria.false: No driver medical event. Injuries caused by the crash do not count.

drug_involved.instructions: The `narrative` states or suspects that a driver was under the influence of drugs or medication, not alcohol.

criteria.true: Drug, narcotic, or medication impairment of a driver is stated or suspected.
criteria.false: No drug involvement. Alcohol-only impairment does not count.

alcohol_involved.instructions: The `narrative` states or suspects that a driver had been drinking alcohol or was intoxicated by alcohol.

criteria.true: Drinking, odour of alcohol, DWI, DUI, or suspected alcohol intoxication of a driver.
criteria.false: No alcohol involvement of a driver is mentioned.

hydroplane.instructions: The `narrative` states that a vehicle hydroplaned or lost traction because of water on the roadway.

criteria.true: Hydroplaning, or loss of traction or control caused by rain, wet road, or standing water.
criteria.false: No loss of traction due to water. Wet conditions alone do not count.

vehicle_defect.instructions: The `narrative` states that a mechanical failure of a vehicle contributed to the crash.

criteria.true: Tire blowout, brake, steering, or other mechanical failure contributed to the crash.
criteria.false: No mechanical failure. Damage caused by the crash does not count.

fatigue.instructions: The `narrative` states that a driver fell asleep, dozed off, was drowsy, or was fatigued.

criteria.true: A driver was asleep, falling asleep, drowsy, tired, or fatigued before the crash.
criteria.false: No sleep or fatigue of a driver is mentioned.

aggression.instructions: The `narrative` describes road rage, aggressive driving directed at another road user, or a confrontation between people involved.

criteria.true: Road rage, brake-checking, chasing, threatening, arguing, or fighting between involved people.
criteria.false: No aggression. A police pursuit, traffic stop, evading police, or leaving the scene does not count.

intentional.instructions: The `narrative` states or suspects that a vehicle was used intentionally to cause the crash.

criteria.true: The crash is described as deliberate, intentional, an assault with a vehicle, or a suicide attempt.
criteria.false: The crash is unintentional, or intent is not mentioned.

wrong_way.instructions: The `narrative` states that a vehicle was traveling the wrong way on a roadway, ramp, or lane.

criteria.true: A vehicle travelled the wrong way or against traffic on a one-way road, divided highway, or ramp.
criteria.false: No wrong-way travel. Crossing the center line during a loss of control does not count.

notes: §6 Step 2 lean screen. Same 10 presence concepts as the full schema, shortened instructions and criteria to hold the token budget near 930. pii_residual is deliberately NOT included: an 11th Noul would add ~9% to every one of 500k Stage-1 calls (~$1.8, over the $19.5 line item) to screen narratives that will never be displayed. §6 Step 1 needs it only for narratives that are quoted or shown publicly, so it ships as its own one-question schema (pii_residual_v1.json) run on display candidates.
